display: Búzios, Cabo Frio & Arraial do Cabo (Costa do Sol)
tagline: Brazil's Costa do Sol — Búzios' glamour peninsula, Cabo Frio's canal city and the 'Brazilian Caribbean' of Arraial do Cabo — three beach capitals a few miles apart by sea, still linked only by summer-jammed roads.
summary: The Costa do Sol (Região dos Lagos) is Rio state's second great coastal playground after the Costa Verde: Búzios with its 20+ beaches and Orla Bardot waterfront, Cabo Frio with the Canal do Itajuru marina district and roughly three million summer visitors, and Arraial do Cabo, whose translucent water draws crowds so heavy the Navy caps its most famous beach at 300 people at a time. Every one of these towns already lives on the water — cruise tenders, escunas, taxi-boats and charter lanchas move hundreds of thousands of people a year — yet there is no scheduled water link between them; everything inter-town crawls by road in peak-season traffic. Foiling-electric vessels fly above the region's famous wind chop, silent and low-wake in a marine extractive reserve, turning the tour circuit into a premium experience and the Búzios–Cabo Frio–Arraial triangle into a 15–50 minute water grid.

demand_signals.label: Cabo Frio summer volume
demand_signals.value: ~3 million visitors in summer 2024/25 (21 Dec–20 Mar); ~700,000 in the réveillon fortnight alone
demand_signals.note: Municipal tourism secretariat figures; Região dos Lagos received ~1.2 million people over the same New Year period
demand_signals.source: Prefeitura de Cabo Frio / Folha dos Lagos

demand_signals.label: Búzios visitor base
demand_signals.note: One of Brazil's top destinations for foreign visitors; ~255 sun days a year

demand_signals.label: Búzios cruise tendering
demand_signals.value: 76,276 cruise passengers tendered ashore in January 2026 alone (26 calls); ~80 calls in the 2025/26 season
demand_signals.note: Búzios is a tender port — every single cruise visitor already arrives across the water, landing at the Píer Central and Porto Veleiro
demand_signals.source: Prefeitura de Búzios (Secretaria de Turismo, Jan 2026)

demand_signals.label: Arraial do Cabo peak crush
demand_signals.value: ~2 million tourists over Carnaval 2025; 20,000+ foreign visitors a year
demand_signals.note: The 'Brazilian Caribbean' — access to its marquee beach is rationed: the Navy caps Praia do Farol at 300 concurrent visitors, reachable only by authorized boats
demand_signals.source: Prefeitura de Arraial do Cabo / Marinha do Brasil (IEAPM Portaria 46/2017)

demand_signals.label: Proven willingness to pay on the water
demand_signals.value: Escuna seats R$70–110; premium small-boat tours from R$180; private lanchas R$1,400–2,700 per outing
demand_signals.note: A large, priced, functioning informal boat economy at all three towns — the demand layer a modern fleet upgrades
demand_signals.source: Operator price lists (Royal Turquesa, Búzios Trip Tour, Don Juan Tour, Enjoy Playa Adventure)

use_cases.title: Modernise the tour-boat habit
use_cases.body: Arraial do Cabo's entire tour economy departs from one marina at Praia dos Anjos under municipal (FIPAC) rules, and Búzios' escunas loop the peninsula's beaches daily. Foiling vessels fly the same circuits smoother, quieter and without diesel wake — a premium tier on top of an adopted habit, not a new behaviour.

use_cases.title: The missing inter-town water link
use_cases.body: Búzios–Cabo Frio (~12 nm) and Cabo Frio–Arraial (~6 nm) move today almost entirely by road, which saturates every summer weekend. A scheduled foiling shuttle turns the triangle into a 15–50 minute water grid between the Píer Central, the Canal do Itajuru and Praia dos Anjos.

use_cases.title: Cruise shore-excursion layer
use_cases.body: Every Búzios cruise passenger already lands by boat. Foiling shuttles waiting at the Píer Central and Porto Veleiro extend a 9-hour port call to Arraial's capped beaches and back with time to spare — a shore excursion no bus can match.

use_cases.title: Marina-based premium charter
use_cases.body: BR Marinas' Marina Porto Búzios and the Canal do Itajuru yacht clubs (Costa Azul, ICRJ Cabo Frio) already homeport a large private-lancha fleet renting at R$1,400–2,700 per day. Silent foiling day-charters across the Costa do Sol slot straight into that market at its existing price points.

journeys.to: Arraial do Cabo (Marina dos Pescadores, Praia dos Anjos)
journeys.today: A van or car down RJ-102/RJ-124 — an hour or more in summer traffic, for two towns that face each other across open water.
journeys.with_navier: A ~50-minute foiling flight along the Costa do Sol shoreline, stepping off at the marina where every Arraial tour begins.

journeys.to: Praia do Farol (Ilha do Cabo Frio)
journeys.today: A diesel escuna or crowded lancha across the Boqueirão to a Navy-protected beach capped at 300 visitors — noisy arrivals in some of Brazil's clearest, most protected water.
journeys.with_navier: A silent, shallow-draft, low-wake hop that matches the conservation regime — precise arrival slots for a rationed beach.

journeys.today: A short but slow summer drive, or a private lancha day-package from the canal marinas at R$1,500–2,100.
journeys.with_navier: A 15–20 minute foiling shuttle out of the canal mouth past Forte São Mateus, straight across the Praia do Forte bight.

journeys.to: Cabo Frio (Canal do Itajuru / Boulevard Canal)
journeys.today: Road only — no scheduled water service has ever linked the two biggest towns of the Região dos Lagos.
journeys.with_navier: A ~35-minute flight around the headlands of Tucuns and Peró, docking on the canal boulevard in the heart of Cabo Frio.

journeys.today: A 2.5–3 hour drive on the Via Lagos, longer on summer Fridays — the classic carioca weekend slog.
journeys.with_navier: A fast hybrid coastal corridor (~79 nm) linking the metro of 13 million to its favourite beach peninsula, no charging infrastructure required en route.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The whole Costa do Sol triangle sits deep inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope: Búzios↔Cabo Frio ~12 nm, Cabo Frio↔Arraial ~6 nm, Búzios↔Arraial ~18 nm, marina spurs of 0.5–4 nm — with marina charging available at BR Marinas Búzios and the Canal do Itajuru clubs. Low wake and near-silence fit the Arraial marine extractive reserve and the capped Praia do Farol.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range opens the corridors beyond the triangle: Rio de Janeiro (Marina da Glória) ~79 nm west, and onward links toward the Angra dos Reis / Ilha Grande network — connecting Rio state's two great coastal playgrounds by water with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

competitive_landscape: The water is already busy — which is the point. At Arraial do Cabo, virtually all tours depart the Marina dos Pescadores at Praia dos Anjos: FIPAC-registered escunas and taxi-boats, the larger vessels carrying up to 80 passengers, at R$70–180 per seat. Búzios runs a daily escuna and catamaran circuit (R$70–110) from the Píer Central and Porto Veleiro, plus cruise tenders landing tens of thousands of passengers a month in season. Cabo Frio's canal marinas homeport a private-lancha fleet renting at R$1,400–2,700 a day. All of it is conventional, diesel and slow, and none of it runs a scheduled inter-town service — strong, priced demand with an obvious modernisation gap.
seasonality: Peak is the austral summer, December–March, when Cabo Frio alone hosts ~3 million visitors and hotel occupancy runs 90%+; Carnaval and réveillon are the crush points. Búzios claims ~255 sun days a year and the cruise season runs October–April. The region's signature ocean feature is the Cabo Frio upwelling — cold, glass-clear water that made Arraial famous. Strong northeast trade winds build afternoon chop and southwest frontal swells cancel conventional open-water tours several days a month; foiling above the chop converts exactly those days, while the Baía dos Anjos, Manguinhos bight and Canal do Itajuru offer sheltered all-weather nodes. No cyclone exposure.
regulatory_note: The Brazilian Navy (Capitania dos Portos do Rio de Janeiro, Delegacia de Cabo Frio) governs vessel certification and crewing; ANTAQ oversees scheduled waterway passenger services. Locally, Arraial do Cabo's tour fleet operates under the municipal FIPAC foundation, whose Resolução 32/2025 consolidated rules and mandatory registration for all passenger vessels at the Marina dos Pescadores. Arraial's waters sit inside the Reserva Extrativista Marinha de Arraial do Cabo (ICMBio) and landings at Praia do Farol are rationed by the Navy's IEAPM (Portaria 46/2017: 300 concurrent visitors, authorized vessels only) — a regime that rewards silent, low-wake, zero-emission craft. Búzios is drafting a management plan for its Parque dos Corais marine park (2026), signalling the same clean-marine direction.
signature_routes: Búzios (Píer Central) ↔ Arraial do Cabo (Marina dos Pescadores) — the Costa do Sol inter-town flagship, ~18 nm
Arraial do Cabo ↔ Praia do Farol (Ilha do Cabo Frio) — silent access to the Navy-capped 'Brazilian Caribbean' beach
Búzios (Píer Central) ↔ Cabo Frio (Canal do Itajuru) — two beach capitals, ~35 minutes by water
Rio de Janeiro (Marina da Glória) ↔ Búzios — the weekend corridor, ~79 nm hybrid line-haul

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates electric foiling as the backbone of resort and inter-island mobility at national scale — the playbook for turning an informal boat economy into a modern water-transit layer.
